attempt_1_failure_detail: vLLM 0.29.0's bundled Pixtral vision-tower integration (used internally by the Mistral3ForConditionalGeneration architecture registry) raised ImportError: cannot import name 'PixtralRotaryEmbedding' from transformers.models.pixtral.modeling_pixtral, against the auto-resolved transformers==5.17.0. Failed during ModelConfig/architecture inspection at engine-config-build time, ~30 seconds in, before any weight download began. Root-caused to an upstream transformers 5.17.0 API change that vLLM 0.29.0's loose 'transformers>=5.10.4' dependency constraint did not protect against.
attempt_2_failure_detail: Corrective action applied: pinned transformers==5.10.4 (vLLM 0.29.0's own stated minimum-tested floor), which resolved the attempt-1 import error -- the model config now inspected successfully and the full ~120.9GB FP8 weight set downloaded and loaded across both H200 GPUs (tensor-parallel-size=2) over ~1076 seconds. The run then failed during vLLM's post-load profiling/dummy-run forward pass with: RuntimeError: Could not find nvcc and default cuda_home='/usr/local/cuda' doesn't exist, raised inside flashinfer/jit/cpp_ext.py while attempting to JIT-compile a FlashInfer kernel for the --attention-backend FLASH_ATTN_MLA backend this architecture's MLA attention requires. The Modal image installed vLLM's Python/CUDA-runtime dependencies but not the full CUDA development toolkit (nvcc), which FlashInfer's JIT compilation path requires. This is a container-image/package-provisioning gap, not a model or vLLM-version defect -- the model itself loaded successfully onto both GPUs before this failure.
